catalog_quote: 4. Foot. Every morpheme that consists of more than one syllable has one predictable stress. Morphemes that consist only of one or two consonants do not have stress. Stress falls on the final syllable of a morpheme that has at least one vowel unless that syllable is V or CV, in which case stress falls on the penultimate syllable; if there is no penultimate syllable, a V or CV morpheme is not stressed. A foot consists of from one to eight (and possibly more) morphemes, including those that carry stress and those that do not. Epenthetic vowels are added according to rule, as outlined below in the section on morphophonemics, in order to shape the string of morphemes into permitted syllable patterns. The foot has a single primary stress, more pronounced than morpheme stress, which falls on the final syllable unless that syllable is V or CV, in which case stress falls on the penultimate sylla…

sources.note: Only other dedicated phonology of Wapishana (segments and syllable structure, non-linear); would independently document the syllable-weight inventory (CVV, CVG, CVC, VC heavy) our 'wcls' field rests on. Low expected yield for stress itself: Santos 2006 sec. 2.4 calls stress 'ainda tão pouco estudado' and cites only Tracy for prior stress facts.
